name: Ehrwalder Alm
kurzbeschreibung: Ehrwalder Alm (1,502 m) at the base of the Wetterstein range is a sunny alpine plateau for families, hikers, and mountain bikers.
preis: Ehrwalder Almbahn cable car round-trip adults approx. €23.00; Z-Ticket valid
oeffnungszeiten: Summer season mid-May to early November daily 08:30 to 16:30; winter December to April
beschreibung:
Overview

The picturesque Ehrwalder Alm spreads across an expansive, sun-blessed high plateau at an altitude of 1,502 meters right at the foot of the Wetterstein rock walls in the Tyrolean Zugspitz Arena. As a time-honoured alpine pasture, the area looks back on centuries of dairy farming and has evolved over generations into a year-round recreation haven for families, hikers, and winter sports fans. In summer, the plateau enchants visitors with lush mountain meadows, blooming alpine rose fields, babbling brooks, and grand panoramic views of the Zugspitze massif, the Mieming Range, and the Ehrwald valley basin. In winter, the area transforms into a family ski resort with reliable snow conditions, while traditional chalets and modern mountain inns welcome guests with warm hospitality and regional delicacies.

Route & Requirements

Ascending to the plateau is effortless, swift, and barrier-free aboard the modern 8-seater gondolas of the Ehrwalder Almbahn departing from Ehrwald. Those preferring to hike can follow the scenic 'Almstraße' or ascend through the romantic Gaistal gorge in about 1.5 hours (approx. 400 meters of elevation). On the plateau itself, strolls and family walks with all-terrain strollers follow wide, gentle gravel trails that require minimal effort. For mountain hikers, the Ehrwalder Alm serves as the prime trailhead for tours to turquoise Lake Seebensee, the Coburger Hütte, or through the untouched Gaistal towards Leutasch. For alpine treks towards the Wetterstein crest, sturdy hiking boots, weatherproof clothing, and surefootedness are essential.

Visit & Arrival

The Ehrwalder Almbahn operates daily from mid-May to early November and from December to April from 08:30 to 16:30. Ascent and descent tickets are available at the valley station; cable car rides are included with the Zugspitz Arena Z-Ticket. Motorists travel via Garmisch-Partenkirchen or over the Fernpass to Ehrwald, where ample free parking is provided at the valley station. By train, the Außerfern Railway runs to Ehrwald station, with direct guest buses connecting to the cable car base.

Tips

Take the classic hike from the Ehrwalder Alm up to scenic Lake Seebensee, whose turquoise water mirrors the sheer limestone walls of the Wetterstein – one of Tyrol's most celebrated photo locations. Stop at the Tirolerhaus at the mountain terminal for crispy Kaiserschmarrn on the sun deck.
